text:
maya (infra): Heads up — noticed weird autoscaler behavior this morning around GPU nodepools in us-west1.
maya (infra): Pods requesting 1xA100 keep getting scheduled to multiple nodes that only have fractional MIG slices, so CA refuses to scale down and we get fragmentation.
maya (infra): Example: job-rt-embed wants 40GB, kube-scheduler places fragments across 3 nodes each with 16GB MIG partitions. pods Pending -> OOM-ish errors later.
samir: ugh. can you paste the scheduler events?
maya (infra): pasted below from kube-events: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  58s (x3 over 2m)  default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 2 node(s) had taint {dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule}.
Normal   TriggeredScaleUp   30s (x2 over 1m)  cluster-autoscaler  Pod triggered scale-up: [{nodegroup/gpu-lg-usw1 1->2 (max:5)}]
Normal   ScaleUp     5s  cluster-autoscaler  Scale-up: setting group gpu-lg-usw1 size to 2
```

jules: are those MIG-enabled instances? which node pool config?
maya (infra): Yes MIG on the A100s. Node pool config: 
```
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-frag-usw1
spec:
  autoscaling:
    enabled: true
    minNodeCount: 1
    maxNodeCount: 6
  gceMachineType: n1-standard-16
  acceleratorConfigs:
  - acceleratorCount: 1
    acceleratorType: nvidia-tesla-a100
  nodeGpus:
    migProfile: "1g.10gb"
```

kevin: ah — we're creating pools with mixed MIG profiles and also allowing time-slicing on some pools. CA treats each node as having fractional resources; it can't coalesce those fragments for a single pod.
kevin: Short term options: 1) create dedicated node pools per MIG profile (e.g., 1g.10gb, 2g.20gb) and label them, 2) use pod affinity/anti-affinity + nodeSelectors to binpack by job type, 3) prevent CA from evicting critical pods with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"`.
samir: Also consider using `--balance-similar-node-groups` + `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false`? Not sure on impact with GPUs.
maya (infra): We already run CA v1.24 with `--balance-similar-node-groups`, but fragmentation still happening. CA will scale up fine but scale-down can't reclaim because leftover small MIG slices are not usable for new big pods.
autoscale-bot: Reminder: scale-down disabled for node pool "gpu-frag-usw1" between 03:00-05:00 UTC due to scheduled tests.
jules: Longer term: either (A) avoid time-sliced GPUs for latency-critical workloads and reserve time-sliced pools for cheap batch inference; or (B) switch to non-MIG mode (full GPU per node) for any workloads that require > single fragment.
kevin: We should also consider building a scheduler predicate/elastic-gpu-adapter that understands MIG packing across nodes? That seems heavy.
maya (infra): Proposal: create two new node pools: `gpu-big-usw1` (no MIG, whole GPU pinned) and `gpu-burst-usw1` (MIG time-slice, preemptible). Add labels `gpu.profile=big` / `gpu.profile=burst`. Update deployment manifests for latency jobs to `nodeSelector: gpu.profile: big` and allow batch jobs to target `burst`.
samir: +1. Also add a CA expander policy to prefer `big` when pods request >=32GB.
jules: For cost, move some low-priority offline evals to `burst` and set `tolerations` for `preemptible` taint.
kevin: I'll draft the node pool terraform change and a short runbook for oncall.
maya (infra): One more: add an alert when fragmentation grows above threshold. For example: metric `gpu.frag_ratio` > 0.6 across cluster -> page ops.
kevin: Can we approximate `gpu.frag_ratio` with: (total free GPU mem in fragments < largest pod request) / total GPU mem? We can iterate.
samir: I'll add a Grafana panel and a prom rule.
maya (infra): TY. Plan: 1) create node pools and labels, 2) update deployments (small batch), 3) monitoring + alerting, 4) revisit CA flags if needed.
jules: Sounds good. If anyone is blocked on quota in us-west1, ping me — we might hit regional GPU limits. :warning:
maya (infra): Will action after lunch and post updates here. :thumbsup:
kevin: tracking in infra board: INFRA-4823.
autoscale-bot: Scale-up event: nodegroup/gpu-big-usw1 increased 1->2 at 1765433500
kevin: update: test deploy passed on `gpu-big-usw1`, pods packed onto single nodes as expected.
